LOCAL TASTE

Named by 4 sources: Wikidata (Wikipedia in many languages), national heritage register, Wikivoyage (English), Wikipedia in Italian

Photo spot: Shoot straight up at the oculus from the center.

Read the story

The Pantheon was rebuilt by the emperor Hadrian around AD 125, and it's the best-preserved building from ancient Rome. It survived because in 609 it became a church, Saint Mary and the Martyrs. Step inside and look up: the dome is still the largest unreinforced concrete dome in the world, 43 meters wide, exactly as high as it is wide. The only light comes through the open hole at the top, the oculus. When it rains, the water falls in and drains through little holes in the floor. The painter Raphael is buried here.

Privacy

Draft, lawyer review before launch. Not yet reviewed by a lawyer; it will be before Kairoute is sold or published in an app store.

Effective November 10, 2026

Kairoute is built to keep your trip yours. This policy explains what the app stores, what it sends, and the choices you have.

What stays on your device
Your trips, itineraries, hotels, cruise details and preferences.
City guides the app has built for you.
Your journal: notes, ratings and photos.

The preview has no accounts. We do not see this information unless you share it.

What is sent to provide the AI guide

When you build a guide, import an itinerary, ask the guide a question or translate a story, the text or photo you provide is sent to our AI provider to produce the answer. Do not include passport numbers, payment details or other sensitive information in itinerary photos.

Location

The preview does not use your location. The full app will ask for permission before using GPS for walking directions and arrival alerts, and you can turn it off at any time.

What we do not do
We do not sell your personal information.
We do not show third-party ads or use advertising trackers.
We do not build a profile of you for marketing.
Sharing a trip

When you share or export a trip, the people you send it to can see everything in it. Shared copies are under their control.

Deleting your data

Delete a single trip from the home screen, or clear everything in Settings, Start over. Uninstalling the app or clearing your browser data also removes it.

Children

Kairoute is not directed to children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect their information.

Changes and contact

If this policy changes, we will update the date above and tell you in the app. Questions: privacy@[your domain].

Effective November 20, 2026

By using Kairoute you agree to these terms. If you do not agree, please do not use the app.

A planning guide with estimated times

Kairoute suggests routes, times, places to eat and stories about the sights. Opening hours, prices, port times, transit and closures change. Always confirm important details with the venue, your cruise line, airline or rail operator.

Getting back on time is your responsibility

Leave-by times, back-by times and countdowns are estimates. Kairoute pads them with spare time (on a port day it plans you back at least 45 minutes before all aboard), but traffic, queues, weather, strikes and changes to timetables can still make a trip take longer.

The official time is always the one your cruise line, airline or rail operator gives you: the ship's all-aboard time, your boarding time or your departure. Kairoute shows the ship's all-aboard time next to its own times so you can check them against each other. Confirm it on the day, as it can change.

You are responsible for being back aboard your ship, at your gate or on your train on time. Kairoute is not liable for missed ships, flights, trains, connections, tours or bookings, or for any costs that follow from them.

AI content

Guides, translations and answers may be written with the help of AI and can contain mistakes. Use your judgment, and do not rely on the app for medical, legal or safety advice.

Stay safe

Watch where you walk, follow local laws and posted rules, and be aware of your surroundings. Do not use the app while driving.

Pantheon

Temple and church · 30 min · Must-see

Local name: Pantheon (Roma)

A 1,900-year-old temple with a perfect dome, now a church.

🤫
Quiet place. Read the story below. Audio plays only after you confirm your earbuds are in.

🎧 Play with earbuds
The story

The Pantheon was rebuilt by the emperor Hadrian around AD 125, and it's the best-preserved building from ancient Rome. It survived because in 609 it became a church, Saint Mary and the Martyrs. Step inside and look up: the dome is still the largest unreinforced concrete dome in the world, 43 meters wide, exactly as high as it is wide. The only light comes through the open hole at the top, the oculus. When it rains, the water falls in and drains through little holes in the floor. The painter Raphael is buried here.

WHAT TO LOOK FOR
The oculus and the beam of sunlight moving across the dome.
The tiny drain holes in the floor.
Raphael's tomb.
